hook.line: She works at TikTok and says the secret to more views in 2026 is SEO.
hook.visual: Woman in a red shirt walking in a TikTok office holding a mic; boxed title 'How to get more views on TikTok using SEO / From a TikTok employee' at the top.

beats.what: Insider claim ('I work at TikTok') with the boxed title and authority subtitle already on screen.
Cut to her seated on a green bench; defines SEO as search engine optimisation.
Big white title 'Good SEO = More reach & search results' sums up the definition.
Punch-in zoom on 'the better the SEO, the more views you can unlock'.
Cut to a new spot in the office for the how-to: add keywords.
Emoji checklist title 'Add keywords to: Scripts / Text On Screen / Captions'.
Punch-in on 'what your niche is or who your audience are'.
Floating keyword examples ('Tech Tips', 'New Tech', 'Tech Advice') appear around her head.
Final cut to a close shot: follow to learn from people who work at TikTok.

why_it_works: Authority in the first two words ('I work at TikTok') plus the 'From a TikTok employee' subtitle makes the tip feel like insider information.
A new location roughly every 6-8 s (5 cuts, plus 3 punch-ins) resets attention without needing B-roll.
Each step is summarised in a big on-screen title (definition, then a 3-item emoji checklist), so the video works muted and is easy to screenshot or save.
The keyword example is shown, not told: the words float around her head as she says them.
weaknesses: Captions sit low (96% of text outside the safe zone) and overlap the account watermark, so they are hard to read.
Generic advice (add keywords) with no proof, number or before/after result.
Quiet mix (about -32 LUFS) for a talking video.
for_robert: Copy the floating-keywords move: when he names examples, have them pop up around his head one by one, and let Fred swim through and bump one, instead of only listing them in a caption.
